text:
NOT DONE. Both halves are blocked for different reasons, each stated precisely so this is actionable rather than vague.

HALF 1 — transport buffers. This is P7.2's work by explicit assignment, not mine. P7.2 (bd-01KYNA5EAA733KTPSK7M1V1JWZ, "Replace Vector[Byte] with ByteVector") cites FrameCodec.scala's `var remaining = buffered ++ input` as its own motivation. The quadratic behaviour is real — a full buffer copy per fed chunk — and so is the ~5x boxing cost of Vector[Byte], and scodec-bits is ALREADY a declared dependency of kernel, core and protocol with ADR 0012 already accepted.

I deliberately did not fix it here. A contained non-quadratic rewrite inside the existing Vector[Byte] representation is possible (accumulate chunks, materialize only at a frame boundary), but it would be thrown away by the representation swap and would mean designing the buffer twice — exactly the duplication this epic's ordering exists to prevent. P7.2 should do it once, in ByteVector terms.

Note for whoever picks up P7.2: it is now UNBLOCKED in a way it was not when written. Its stated gate was P7.3 (the scodec-bits dependency decision), which is closed, and its downstream P6f.12 now additionally depends on P8.D1-D5, all of which are closed. The public shape has settled, so the representation swap no longer risks being invalidated by an API change.

HALF 2 — batched result reads. A genuine feature, not cleanup, and larger than it sounds. G2 delivered a CEILING on simultaneous exchanges, which fixes the operational hazard (a 100-element batch no longer opens 100 SSH processes per tick). Actual batching means one exchange returning several results, which needs:
  - a new AgentMethod plus request/response DTOs and codecs
  - golden wire fixtures re-pinned
  - an agent-side handler
  - a client method on SshAgentApi and AgentApi
  - a rewire of RemoteBatchHandle.await, which today polls each element independently on its own backoff, into a batch-level poller that collects pending reads per tick

That last item is the substance: it is a redesign of the await loop, not an addition beside it. Roughly six files including wire fixtures.

Sequencing recommendation: do it AFTER P7.2. The new batch-read DTOs are wire types, and adding them before the representation swap means hand-writing their codecs twice — the same constraint that put P6f.12 after P7.2 in the original P7 epic.
